verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              सत्यं दमं क्षमा प्रज्ञा प्रशंसन्ति पितामह । विद्वांसो मनुजा लोके कथमेतन्मतं तव ॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said 0 grandfather, learmed men praise truth, self-control, forgiveness and wisdom. What is your opinion about these virtues?

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              अत्र ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम् । साध्यानामिह संवादं हंसस्य च युधिष्ठिर ॥२॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Regarding it I shall recite to you an old narrative, O Yudhishthira, of the discourse between the Sadhyas and a Swan.

verses.sanskrit: हंसो भूत्वाऽथ सौवर्णस्त्वजो नित्यः प्रजापतिः । स वै पर्येति लोकांस्त्रीनथ साध्यानुपागमत् ॥३॥
verses.english: Once on a time the uncreate and eternal Lord of all creatures, assuming the form of a golden Swan, passed through the three worlds till in course of his ramblings he came upon the Sadhyas.

verses.sanskrit: साध्या ऊचुः । शकुने वयं स्म देवा वै साध्यास्त्वामनुयुंक्ष्महे । पृच्छामस्त्वां मोक्षधर्मं भवांश्च किल मोक्षवित् ॥४॥
verses.english: The Saddhyas said 0 lord, we are the gods called Sadhyas. We like to question you. Indeed, we would ask you about the religion of liberation. You are well acquainted with it.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुतोऽसि नः पण्डितो धीरवादी साधुशब्दश्चरते ते पतत्रिन् । किं मन्यसे श्रेष्ठतमं द्विज त्वं कस्मिन्मनस्ते रमते महात्मन् ॥५॥
verses.english: We have heard, O bird, that you are endued with great learning, and eloquent and wise of speech. O bird, what do you think is the highest of all objects? O great one, in what does your mind find pleasure?

verses.sanskrit: तन्नः कार्यं पक्षिवर प्रशाधि यत्कार्याणां मन्यसे श्रेष्ठमेकम् । यत्कृत्वा वै पुरुषः सर्वबन्धैर्विमुच्यते विहगेन्द्रेह शीघ्रम् ॥६॥
verses.english: Do you, therefore, O foremost of birds, instruct us as to what that one act is which you consider as the foremost of all acts, and by doing which, O king of birds, one may soon be freed from all fetters.

verses.sanskrit: हंस उवाच । इदं कार्यममृताशाः शृणोमि तपो दमः सत्यमात्माभिगुप्तिः । ग्रन्थीन्विमुच्य हृदयस्य सर्वान् प्रियाप्रिये स्वं वशमानयीत ॥७॥
verses.english: The Swan said O nectar-drinking ones, I have heard that one should follow these, viz., penances, selfcontrol, truth, and subjugation of the mind. Losing all the knots of the heart, one should also bring under his control both what is pleasant and what is unpleasant.

verses.sanskrit: नारुन्तुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत । ययाऽस्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत न तां वदेदुषतीं पापलोक्याम् ॥८॥
verses.english: One should not cut the vitals of others. One should not utter cruel words. One should never receive scriptural lectures from a mean person. one should never utter such words as pain others, as make others miserable, and as lead to hell.

verses.sanskrit: वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्पतन्ति यैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि । परस्य नामर्मसु ते पतन्ति तान्पण्डितो नावसृजेत्परेषु ॥९॥
verses.english: Wordy arrows fall from the lips. Pierced therewith one burns always. Those arrows do not cut any other part than the very vitals of the person aimed. Hence he who is a learned man, should never aim them at others.

verses.sanskrit: परश्चेदेनमतिवादबाणैर्भृशं विध्येच्छम एवेह कार्यः । संरोष्यमाणः प्रतिहष्यते यः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परस्य ॥१०॥
verses.english: If a person deeply cuts a wise man with wordy arrows, the wise man should remain silent. The man who, though sought to be angered, rejoices without giving way to anger, takes away from the provoker all his merits,

verses.sanskrit: क्षेपायमाणमभिषङ्गव्यलीकं निगृह्णाति ज्वलितं यश्च मन्युम् । अदृष्टचेता मुदितोऽनसूयुः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परेषाम् ॥११॥
verses.english: That man of virtuous soul, who, full of joy and shom of malice, control his burning ire which, if indulged, would lead him to speak ill of others and verily become his enemy, takes away the merits of others.

verses.sanskrit: आक्रुश्यमानो न वदामि किंचित् क्षमाम्यहं ताड्यमानश्च नित्यम् । श्रेष्ठं ह्येतद्यत्क्षममाहुरार्याः सत्यं तथैवार्जवमानृशंस्यम् ॥१२॥
verses.english: As for myself, I never answer when another speaks ill of me. If attacked, I always forgive the assault. The righteous hold that forgiveness, truth, sincerity and compassion are the foremost (of all virtues).

verses.sanskrit: वेदस्योपनिषत्सत्यं सत्यस्योपनिषद्दमः । दमस्योपनिषन्मोक्ष एतत्सर्वानुशासनम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: Truth is the essence of the Vedas. The essence of Truth is self-control. The essence of self-control is Liberation. This is the teaching of all the scriptures.

verses.sanskrit: वाचो वेगं मनसः क्रोधवेगं विधित्सावेगमुदरोपस्थवेगम् । एतान्वेगान्यो विषहेदुदीर्णांस्तं मन्येऽहं ब्राह्मणं वै मुनिं च ॥१४॥
verses.english: I know that person as a Brahmana and Muni who governs the rising impulse of speech, the impulse of anger appearing in the mind, the impulse to thirst, and the impulses of the stomach and the organ of pleasure.

verses.sanskrit: अक्रोधनः क्रुध्यतां वै विशिष्टस्तथा तितिक्षुरतितिक्षोर्विशिष्टः । अमानुषान्मानुषो वै विशिष्टस्तथाऽज्ञानाज्ज्ञानविद्वै विशिष्टः ॥१५॥
verses.english: One who does not give way to anger is superior to one who does. One who practises renunciation is superior to one who does nol. One who possesses the virtues of manhood is superior to one who has them not. One who has knowledge is superior to one who has not got it.

verses.sanskrit: आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रुश्येन्मन्युरेनं तितिक्षतः । आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति ॥१६॥
verses.english: Assailed with harsh words, one should not assail in return. Indeed, one who, under such circumstances, renounces anger, succeeds in burning the assailer and taking away all his merits.

verses.sanskrit: यो नात्युक्तः प्राह रूक्षं प्रियं वा यो वा हतो न प्रतिहन्ति धैर्यात् । पापं च यो नेच्छति तस्य हन्तुस्तस्येह देवाः स्पृहयन्ति नित्यम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: That person who when attacked with harsh words, does not utter a harsh word in reply, who when lauded does not say what is pleasant to him who praise, who is gifted with such fortitude as not to strike in return when struck and not to even wish evil to the striker, finds his company always sought after by the gods.

verses.sanskrit: पापीयसः क्षमेतैव श्रेयसः सदृशस्य च । विमानितो हतोत्क्रुष्ट एवं सिद्धिं गमिष्यति ॥१८॥
verses.english: A sinful man should be forgiven as if he were righteous by one who is insulted, struck, and calumniated. By acting in this way one gains success.

verses.sanskrit: सदाऽहमार्यान्निभृतोऽप्युपासे न मे विधित्सोत्सहते न रोषः । न वाप्यहं लिप्समानः परैमि न चैव किञ्चिद्विषयेण यामि ॥१९॥
verses.english: Though all my objects have been fulfilled, yet I always wait respectfully on the righteous. I have no thirst. My anger has been suppressed. Seduced by covetousness I do not deviate from the path of virtue. I do not also approach any one with prayers for riches.

verses.sanskrit: नाहं शप्तः प्रतिशपामि कंचिद्दमं द्वारं ह्यमृतस्येह वेद्मि । गुह्यं ब्रह्म तदिदं ब्रवीमि न मानुषाच्छ्रेष्ठतरं हि किंचित् ॥२०॥
verses.english: If cursed I do not curse in return. I know that self-control is the door of immortality. I disclose to you a great mystery. There is no position that is superior to that of humanity.

verses.sanskrit: निर्मुच्यमानः पापेभ्यो घनेभ्य इव चन्द्रमाः । विरजाः कालमाकाङ्क्षन्धीरो धैर्येण सिद्ध्यति ॥२१॥
verses.english: Freed from sin like the Moon from misty clouds, the wise man, shining in resplendence, acquires success by patiently waiting for his time.

verses.sanskrit: यः सर्वेषां भवति ह्यर्चनीय उत्सेधनस्तम्भ इवाभिजातः । यस्मै वाचं सुप्रसन्नां वदन्ति स वै देवान्गच्छति संयतात्मा ॥२२॥
verses.english: A person of controlled soul, who becomes the object of worship with all by becoming the foremost of the pillars of the universe, and to whom only agreeable words are addressed by all, acquires the companionship of the gods.

verses.sanskrit: न तथा वक्तुमिच्छन्ति कल्याणान्पुरुषे गुणान् । यथैषां वक्तमिच्छन्ति नैर्गुण्यमनुयुञ्जकाः ॥२३॥
verses.english: Revilers never speak of the merits of a person as readily as they speak of his demerits.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य वाङ्मनसी गुप्ते सम्यक्प्रणिहिते सदा । वेदास्तपश्च त्यागश्च स इदं सर्वमाप्नुयात् ॥२४॥
verses.english: That person whose speech and mind are properly controlled and always devoted to the Supreme, gets the fruits of the Vedas, Penances, and Renunciation.

verses.sanskrit: आक्रोशनविमानाभ्यां नाबुधान्बोधयेद्बुधः । तस्मान्न वर्धयेदन्यं न चात्मानं विहिंसयेत् ॥२५॥
verses.english: The wise man should never revile (in return) those who have no merit, by speaking out their dispraise and by insults. He should not extol others and should never injure themselves.

verses.sanskrit: अमृतस्येव संतृप्यदेवमानस्य पण्डितः । सुखं ह्यवमतः शेते योऽवमन्ता स नश्यति ॥२६॥
verses.english: The wise and learned man considers revilement as nectar. Reviled, he sleeps without anxiety. The reviler, on the other hand, meets with destruction.

verses.sanskrit: यत्क्रोधनो यजति यद्ददाति यद्वा तपस्तप्यति यज्जुहोति । वैवस्वतस्तद्धरतेऽस्य सर्वं मोघः श्रमो भवति हि क्रोधनस्य ॥२७॥
verses.english: The sacrifices that one celebrates angrily, the gifts one makes in angrily, the penances one practices angrily, and the offerings and libations one makes to the sacred fire angrily, are such that their merits are robbed by Yama. The toil of an angry man becomes entirely frutile.

verses.sanskrit: चत्वारि यस्य द्वाराणि सुगुप्तान्यमरोत्तमाः । उपस्थमुदरं हस्तौ वाक्चतुर्थी स धर्मवित् ॥२८॥
verses.english: You foremost of immortals, that person is said to be conversant with virtue whose four doors, viz., the organ of generation, the stoinach, the two arms, and speech, are well governed.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं दमं ह्यार्जवमानृशंस्यं धृतिं तितिक्षामतिसेवमानः । स्वाध्यायनित्योऽस्पृहयन्परेषामेकान्तशील्यूर्ध्वगतिर्भवेत्सः ॥२९॥
verses.english: That person who, always practising truth and self-control and sincerity and mercy and patience and renunciation, becomes devoted to the study of the Vedas, does not covet others possession, and pursues what is good with a singleness of purpose, succeeds in going to heaven.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वांश्चैनाननुचरन्वत्सवच्चतुरः स्तनान् । न पावनतमं किंचित्सत्यादध्यगमं क्वचित् ॥३०॥
verses.english: Like a calf sucking all the four teets of its dam's udders, one should devote himself to the practice of all these virtues. I do not know whether anything exists more sacred than Truth.

verses.sanskrit: आचक्षेऽहं मनुष्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः प्रतिसंचरन् । सत्यं स्वर्गस्य सोपानं पारावारस्य नौरिव ॥३१॥
verses.english: Having walked among both human beings and the gods, I say that Truth is the only means for reaching heaven even as a ship is the only means for crossing deep.

verses.sanskrit: यादृशैः सन्निवसति यादृशांश्चोपसेवते । यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः ॥३२॥
verses.english: A person becomes like those with whom he lives, and like those whom he respects, and like to what he wishes to be.

verses.sanskrit: यदि सन्तं सेवति यद्यसन्तं तपस्विनं यदि वा स्तेनमेव । वासो यथा रंगवशं प्रयाति तथा स तेषां वशमभ्युपैति ॥३३॥
verses.english: If a person waits respectfully on him who is good, or him who is otherwise, if he waits respectfully on a sage endued with ascetic merit or on a thief, passes under his control and gets his colour like a piece of cloth catching the dye in which it is washed.

verses.sanskrit: सदा देवाः साधुभिः संवदन्ते न मानुषं विषयं यान्ति द्रष्टुम् । नेन्दुः समः स्यादसमो हि वायुरुच्चावचं विषयं यः स वेद ॥३४॥
verses.english: The gods always talk with those who are good and wise. They, therefore, never entertain the desire for even seeing the enjoyments in which men take pleasure. The person who knows that all objects of enjoyment are subject to changes, has few rivals, and is superior to the very Moon and Wind.

verses.sanskrit: अदुष्टं वर्तमाने तु हृदयान्तरपूरुषे । तेनैव देवाः प्रीयन्ते सतां मार्गस्थितेन वै ॥३५॥
verses.english: When the Purusha that lives in one's heart is pure, and walks in the path of the righteous, the gods take a pleasure in him.

verses.sanskrit: शिश्नोदरे ये निरताः सदैव स्तेना नरा वाक्परुषाश्च नित्यम् । अपेतदोषानपि तान्विदित्वा दूराद्देवाः सम्परिवर्जयन्ति ॥३६॥
verses.english: The gods shun from a distance those who are always devoted to the gratification of their senses of pleasure and the stomach, who are given to thieving, and who always indulge in harsh words, even if they expiate their offences by performing the proper rites.

verses.sanskrit: न वै देवा हीनसत्त्वेन तोष्याः सर्वाशिना दुष्कृतकर्मणा वा । सत्यव्रता ये तु नराः कृतज्ञा धर्मे रतास्तैः सह सम्भजन्ते ॥३७॥
verses.english: The god are never gratified with one of mean soul, with one who observes no restraint in the matter of food, and with one who is of sinful deeds. On the other hand, the gods associate with those men who observe the vow of truth, who are grateful, and who are engaged in the practice of virtue.

verses.sanskrit: अव्याहृतं व्याहृताच्छ्रेय आहुः सत्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तद्द्वितीयम् । धर्मं वदेद्व्याहृतं तत्तृतीयं प्रियं वदेद्व्याहृतं तच्चतुर्थम् ॥३८॥
verses.english: Silence is better than speech. To speak the truth is better than silence. To speak, again, truth what is connected with virtue is better than to speak the truth. To speak what, besides being true and righteous is agrecable, is better than to speak truth connected with virtue.

verses.sanskrit: साध्या ऊचुः। केनायमावृतो लोकः केन वा न प्रकाशते । केन त्यजति मित्राणि केन स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥३९॥
verses.english: The Saddhyas said, By what is this world covered? Why does one fail to shine? For what cause do people renounce their friends? Why do people fail to go to heaven.

verses.sanskrit: हंस उवाच । अज्ञानेनावृतो लोको मात्सर्यान्न प्रकाशते । लोभात्त्यजति मित्राणि संगात्स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥४०॥
verses.english: The world is covered by Ignorance. Men fail to shine on account of malice. People renounce friends, actuated by covetousness. Men fail to attain to heaven on account of attachment.

verses.sanskrit: साध्या ऊचुः । कः स्विदेको रमते ब्राह्मणानां कः स्विदेको बहुभिर्जोषमास्ते । कः स्विदेको बलवान्दुर्बलोऽपि कः स्विदेषां कलहं नान्ववैति ॥४१॥
verses.english: Who alone among the Brahmanas is always happy? Who alone amongst them can practise the vow of silence though living in the midst of many? Who alone amongst them, though weak, is still considered as strong? And who alone amongst them does not quarrel.

verses.sanskrit: हंस उवाच । प्राज्ञ एको रमते ब्राह्मणानां प्राज्ञश्चैको बहुभिर्जोषमास्ते । प्राज्ञ एको बलवान्दुर्बलोऽपि प्राज्ञ एषां कलहं नान्ववैति ॥४२॥
verses.english: He alone amongst the Brahmanas who is endued with wisdom is always happy. He alone. amongst the Brahmanas who is endued with wisdom, succeeds in practising the vow of silence though living in the midst of many. He alone amongst the Brahmanas who is endued with wisdom, thought actually weak, is considered as strong. He alone amongst them who has wisdom succeeds in avoiding quarrel.

verses.sanskrit: साध्या ऊचुः। किं ब्राह्मणानां देवत्वं किं च साधुत्वमुच्यते । असाधुत्वं च किं तेषां किमेषां मानुषं मतम् ॥४३॥
verses.english: The Saddhyas said Wherein lies the divinity of the Brahmanas? In what their purity? In what their impurity? And in what their status of humanity?

verses.sanskrit: हंस उवाच । स्वाध्याय एषां देवत्वं व्रतं साधुत्वमुच्यते । असाधुत्वं परीवादो मृत्युर्मानुष्यमुच्यते ॥४४॥
verses.english: The Swan said The divinity of the Brahmanas consists in the study of the Vedas. Their purity is in their status of humanity?

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              संवाद इत्ययं श्रेष्ठः साध्यानां परिकीर्तितः । क्षेत्रं वै कर्मणां योनिः सद्भावः सत्यमुच्यते ॥४५॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Thus have I recited to you the excellent discourse between the Saddhyas (and the Swan). The body is the origin of acts, and existence or individual Soul is truth.
